desk.headline: Core FFO $1.71 a share, slightly above estimates, but revenue fell after California sale; full-year Core FFO range narrowed, same-property outlook cut
results: Property revenue fell 4% to $381.1m, mainly because Camden sold its California portfolio; Core FFO was $1.71 a share, beating the company's own $1.69 midpoint.
GAAP EPS jumped to $8.71 thanks to a roughly $1.0bn gain on selling 11 California communities for about $1.6bn, partly offset by an $86.4m land impairment.
Same property revenue was flat and NOI slipped 0.2%; new leases were signed 2.0% below the old rent while renewals rose 3.6%.
Bought three communities in Tampa, Charlotte and Nashville for $305.2m and repurchased $50.0m of shares at $105.34 on average.
Liquidity of about $1.8bn at quarter end; about $0.9bn of sale proceeds repaid the credit line and commercial paper.

guidance.summary: Camden kept its 2026 Core FFO midpoint at $6.75 but narrowed the range, and nudged FFO up. It cut its same property revenue and NOI growth outlook after a weak September, and gave Q4 Core FFO of $1.63–1.67.

points: Management said traffic dropped more than expected in September, forcing rent cuts, which is why the same property revenue outlook was lowered.
Concessions from competing new buildings stayed stubborn, from about three weeks free in West Palm Beach to two months in Austin.
Signed new leases improved sharply in October versus September; renewal offers for December and January average about 4.5%.
Southeast Florida, Atlanta, Dallas and Houston performed best; Denver and Nashville lagged, and developments there are on hold.
Management called its own shares the best value it sees for investment, backing continued buybacks.

watch: Whether October's better new-lease trend holds through the seasonally weak winter months.
Concession levels in Austin, Denver and Nashville.
Use of remaining sale proceeds: buybacks ($247.9m authorisation left) versus acquisitions.
